title: Not copying the composer
summary: Allen notes Hug does not copy Jelly Roll or Bix; Hug says to be inspired, not copy.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: One thing I've noticed is that you don't play things like the, say, the composer and performer, like Johnny Rowe or Biggs. You never quite copied them by any means.

A lot of times, if you sit there and analyze it, you'll see that Allman will even rearrange the structure of a piece, or he'll play one strain quite differently, in a different order. I'm trying to say. Yes, that's right.

I do. I don't think that you should try to copy the composer, because then you kind of lose something when you do this, because they can only be the composer. You can't copy him. You know, you can't. I never like to hear anybody say, I copied such and such a person. You know. Mm-hmm. I was inspired by him. Yeah. Something like that, you know. That's true. Mm-hmm.
